text: In our build and the release Agello ships, with the executor's own sampler (SessionConfig::UseExternalSampler false, the default; the C++ runtime, the C API and the Swift wrapper never set it, and only Google's web package, which our tree removed, passes a caller's useExternalSampler through), LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::Decode keeps the last token of every decode step or MTP round as the pending input token, counted in current_step but not yet written to the KV cache; when that token is a stop token, Tasks' stop filter drops it from the text and the decode loop ends, so after a reply that ended on a stop token as the last token of its step or round, the stop token is the executor's pending token. In our build it also stays pending when an MTP round emitted tokens after it, which DecodeOneStep rolls back (ours: e62e6ff1).

text: A pending token produced by decode is a TokenData holding only its id (the executor looks up embeddings only for a prefill's last token and, in GetTokenToDecode, for the token about to be decoded), and FillInputBufferWithToken writes a token without embedding as its int32 id in the first 4 bytes of the input and zeros after it. In our build, PrefillInternal first looks up the embeddings and per-layer embeddings of a pending token that has none (LookupPendingTokenEmbeddings; ours: a82611eb), so for the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B files, whose prefill signatures take embeddings and per-layer embeddings rather than token ids, the stop token that the next prefill writes first gets its own embedding. In the release Agello ships it gets the id-and-zeros row in both inputs instead, so its KV entry is not computed from '<turn|>'.

text: When an MTP round emits the stop token before its last emitted token, our build's DecodeOneStep::Run moves the executor's current_step back by the number of tokens after the stop token, so the stop token stays the pending token, as after a single-token step (ours: e62e6ff1). In the release Agello ships it moves current_step back by sequence_length - step, which drops the tokens after the stop token and the stop token itself; the next prefill then re-pends the token before the stop token (as an id-only TokenData, rewriting its position from an id-and-zeros row), so neither '<turn|>' nor the '\n' after it is in the KV cache at that turn boundary.

The release Agello ships (6da75396 tasks.cc:363-373) still moves back by sequence_length - step, dropping the stop token, and re-pends the token before it id-only. So the claim now holds only for the release.

In the release Agello ships, the file template renders '<tool_call|><turn|>\n<|tool_response>' and later renders put '<|turn>model\n' before the answer, so the KV cache holds '<tool_call|>', the stop token's slot (an id-and-zeros row), then '<|tool_response>response:...<tool_response|>', and the answer without that header.

text: Conversation::GetTokenCount returns the executor's current_step, which counts the pending token (ProcessedTokens::TokenCount is the processed tokens plus one when a token is pending). Compared with the token count of the Gemma 4 file template's render of the same history (assuming the model's tokens equal the render's encoding of its text), in our build it is 1 lower for each reply without reasoning that ended with its stop token pending, except a tool-call reply that stopped on '<|tool_response>', which counts equal, and equal after a reasoning refill. In the release Agello ships it is 1 lower for a tool-call reply too, 2 lower instead when an MTP round emitted the stop token before its last token, and a further 3 lower for an answer generated right after a tool response without reasoning (the '<|turn>model\n' later renders put before it).
formula: render '<turn|>\n' = 2 tokens (106, 107) vs 1 cache slot -> -1 per reply; MTP stop before the round's last token: 0 slots -> -2; answer after a tool response: '<|turn>model\n' (105, 4368, 107) absent -> -3 more; reasoning refill writes the render's tokens -> 0

text: For the Gemma 4 E2B/E4B files the executor's max_num_tokens equals the allocated context N (the context target is maxNumTokens below 32,003, else 32,000, and ClampMaxNumTokens lowers a larger maxNumTokens to the state's entries); a plain decode step writes only position current_step - 1 and Tasks::Decode stops once current_step reaches max_num_tokens, so plain decode never writes past position N - 1.

text: In our build and the release Agello ships (ours: 3fa97211, 2026-10-24), Decode runs an MTP round only when MtpRoundFitsCache holds: its verify positions p..p+3, with p = current_step - 1 when the drafter is primed (or a round was deferred) and p = current_step after a priming step, must end below the state's entries N; otherwise it decodes a plain step and counts mtp_skipped_cache_end. So no round verifies past position N - 1. Before that commit nothing on the MTP path compared them: a primed round could reach position N + 1 and a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache N + 3.
formula: primed: loop continues only while c <= N - 1, p = c - 1, last position p + 3 = c + 2 <= N + 1; priming: a prefill leaves c <= N (X-GAP-008), the priming step writes c - 1, Draft gets position c, last position c + 3 <= N + 3

original_text: In agello-next and the v0.18.0 source, nothing on the MTP path compares the verify positions with the cache size (Tasks::Decode, LlmLiteRtCompiledModelExecutorBase::Decode, EnsureMtpDrafterLoaded and LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft have no such check): a round runs at the first decode after a prefill and whenever the decode loop continues (current_step < max_num_tokens), and its verify run covers positions p..p+3 with p = current_step - 1 in a primed round and p = current_step (taken before the priming step) in a priming round; with N allocated positions (0..N-1), a primed round reaches position N + 1 at most and a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache to N reaches N + 3.

text: On the GPU in our build (ours: LiteRT 362759838), the verify run's key and value writes at positions at or beyond the cache's size are skipped: the add_values_to_cache kernel returns when params[0] + X >= cache_size or >= params[1] (non-ring form), and cache_size is an odml.cache_update attribute that LiteRT rewrites from 32003 to the allocated context, so positions beyond the end are not stored; since 3fa97211 (2026-10-24) no MTP round reaches them.

text: In our build and the release Agello ships, PrepareVerifierInputBuffers fills the verify signature's attention mask (BOOL[1, 1, 4, N] for E4B after the context rewrite) on the CPU with FillAttentionMask from p for 4 rows, and for a causal mask (the Gemma 4 files have no executor metadata, so causal) FillAttentionMask fills row k up to column p + k + 1 without clamping to N; a round runs only when p + 3 < N (MtpRoundFitsCache, ours: 3fa97211), so the fill stays inside the 4N-byte tensor. Before 2026-10-24 a round near the end filled p + 4 - N bytes past it: at most 2 in a primed round and 4 in a priming round right after a prefill that filled the cache.
formula: last row ends at element 3N + (p + 3) + 1 = 3N + p + 4; past the end by 3N + p + 4 - 4N = p + 4 - N; primed p <= N - 2 -> <= 2; priming p <= N -> <= 4

text: Before our guard (3fa97211, 2026-10-24), where the verify-mask overrun landed depended on the mask's buffer: when no GPU consumer registers requirements for a BOOL mask, LiteRT's compiled model falls back to host-memory requirements, so the CreateInputBuffer call LiteRT-LM makes returns a host buffer, which LiteRT allocates with posix_memalign of the buffer size plus XNN_EXTRA_BYTES and zero-fills that tail (XNN_EXTRA_BYTES is 16 when LiteRT is built without its CPU path, XNNPACK's own value otherwise); which buffer type the verify mask gets on Metal, and what a write past a Metal buffer's tensor size hits, were not traced.

text: In our build and in the release Agello ships, the C API's conversation stream callback (CreateConversationCallback in c/conversation.cc) turns the first error status it receives into a final chunk with the error text, or the empty message into a final chunk without error, and then drops every later message, error or not (ours: 8acc748c); a send therefore gets one final chunk however many terminal events the conversation layer produces.

Commit 8acc748c (2026-10-24, 'C API: one final chunk per conversation send [4.1b]'). The stateless v0.18.0 callback is gone from the shipped build.
original_text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, the C API's conversation stream callback (CreateConversationCallback in c/conversation.cc) turns every error status it receives into a chunk with is_final true and the error text, and the empty message into a final chunk without error; it keeps no state, so it passes on every terminal event the conversation layer produces.

text: In our build and in the release Agello ships, for a Gemma 4 conversation with tools in its preface, one tool-call block that the FC parser rejects is reported to the C layer's callback as an error at least twice for the same send: when the block's end fence streams, the internal callback's SendMessage passes the failed ToMessage status (InvalidArgument, because return_error_on_parse_failure defaults to true and neither the C API nor Swift changes it) and decoding goes on; at the end of decode SendCompleteMessage parses the whole reply again and fails on the same block. The C stream callback passes on only the first as a final error chunk and drops the rest (ours: 8acc748c).

The 2026-11-17 Gemma 4 tool commits (9a84a518, 586e2e4c) change the template and the first token after a tool response, not this path. New: CreateConversationCallback (c/conversation.cc:45-86) ends after the first error, so only one final chunk reaches the binding (8acc748c); its comment says a rejected call can report up to three errors (a failing flush of unsent text in SendCompleteMessage adds one), hence 'at least twice'.
original_text: In LiteRT-LM agello-next and v0.18.0, for a Gemma 4 conversation with tools in its preface, one tool-call block that the FC parser rejects produces two error chunks with is_final true for the same send: when the block's end fence streams, the internal callback's SendMessage passes the failed ToMessage status (InvalidArgument, because return_error_on_parse_failure defaults to true and neither the C API nor Swift changes it) to the user callback and the stream goes on; at the end of decode SendCompleteMessage parses the whole reply again, fails on the same block, and sends a second error.

text: In the Swift wrapper of our build and of the release Agello ships, each native send of a stream finds its StreamContext through StreamTable by an integer ID passed as callback_data, not a retained pointer: an error chunk or the final chunk retires the ID, the context finishes the stream once (later finishes do nothing), and a chunk for a retired ID returns without touching anything (ours: 4ca2cf33). A second terminal chunk for the same send can't reach freed memory; the C layer also sends only one (ours: 8acc748c).
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, the gap is closed: swift/ConversationStream.swift at b7b856a0 (new file, 4ca2cf33, 2026-10-16, also in 6da75396): StreamContext.finish ends once under a lock (101-159); StreamTable registers IDs that are never reused and retires them (221-255); handleStreamChunk returns when the ID has no entry, retires it on an error or a final chunk, and finishes the context (273-336); sendToStream registers the context and passes UnsafeMutableRawPointer(bitPattern: id) as callback_data (Conversation.swift:623-639). The release's files differ only in a header comment and 'sending' on yield. The C callback's 'ended' flag (8acc748c) drops later finals as well.
original_text: Both the Swift wrapper Agello ships (85b1a776) and the one at the agello-next pin release the StreamContext retained for a send on every chunk that carries an error, whatever is_final says, as well as on the first final chunk, and sendMessageStream keeps no other reference to the context once the stream has started; a second error chunk for the same send therefore reads the context through takeUnretainedValue and releases it again after the first release freed it, a use-after-free and over-release on LiteRT-LM's thread.

text: The other terminal paths of the conversation layer deliver one terminal event per send: SendCompleteMessage returns after reporting an extraction or parse error without sending the end sentinel; the internal callback's error, cancelled, failed and token-limit-error branches each make one user callback and return; and in our build, when the channel-filter refill reports an error itself, the deferred end sentinel is suppressed.

text: In the release Agello ships (agello-one-20261115, whose llg_constraint.cc is Google's), LlgConstraint::ComputeNext commits the token into the llguidance constraint object of the state it is given (llg_commit_token on that state's pointer) and returns a copy of that state, which shares the same object through a shared_ptr; only Start() clones a fresh object, so every state derived from one Start() is the same mutable llguidance matcher. In our build (ours: 1382157b, 2026-11-17), ComputeNext clones the given state's matcher and commits into the clone, leaving the given state as it was, and each state's owner keeps the mask llguidance computed for it.

The release's llg_constraint.cc/.h equal Google's base (66-91: commit into the given state's pointer, return a copy sharing it). Old claim holds only for the release; corrected for both.

text: In an MTP round with an llguidance constraint, RunDraftingLoop computes each draft's mask from the current state and then commits the draft with ComputeNext, and RunVerification computes the four row masks from the verified state and the three draft states. In the release Agello ships, those states are one matcher, so by verification all point to the matcher after drafts d1, d2 and d3: verifier rows 0 to 2 get the mask for the position after d3 instead of their own position, and only row 3 is right. In our build each state has a matcher of its own (ours: 1382157b), so each row gets its own position's mask.
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: drafter logic the same in both: RunDraftingLoop ComputeMask then ComputeNext per draft (pin 922-1005, release 540-610), RunVerification masks from constraint_state_ and each draft state (pin 1254-1300, release 703-750). What differs is ComputeNext (X-GAP-019): shared matcher in the release, a clone per state in our build (1382157b). Our build's drafter can also skip masks when RoundNeedsNoMasks (282-300). Corrected per build.
original_text: In an MTP round with an llguidance constraint (agello-next and v0.18.0), RunDraftingLoop computes each draft's mask from the current state and then commits the draft with ComputeNext, so by verification the verified state and the three draft states all point to the matcher after drafts d1, d2 and d3; RunVerification computes all four row masks from those states, so verifier rows 0 to 2 get the mask for the position after d3 instead of their own position, and only row 3 is right.

text: After verification, LlmLiteRtMtpDrafter::Draft sets the verified state to draft state n and commits the bonus token. In the release Agello ships, draft state n is the shared matcher already holding d1 to d3, so the matcher ends at verified tokens + d1 d2 d3 + bonus whatever n is; that matches the emitted tokens only when all 3 drafts are accepted; after a rejection the matcher holds rejected drafts, later masks are computed from that state, and the bonus commit can fail, making Draft return InternalError ('Failed to commit token'). In our build draft state n holds only the verified tokens and d1 to dn, and the bonus is committed into a clone (ours: 1382157b), so the state matches the emitted tokens.
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: Draft's update after verification is the same in both (pin 1480-1500, release 808-826: constraint_state_ = draft_constraint_states[n - 1], then ComputeNext(bonus), Start() when ended). With the release's ComputeNext (Google's, 66-91) every draft state is the one matcher; with ours (80-102) each draft state is its own clone. Corrected per build.

text: The priming step is consistent (our build and the release Agello ships): the priming plain decode is masked by ConstrainedDecoder's own state, a separate Start() clone that DecodeLogitsImpl doesn't advance with the prompt's last token (ran_decode is false after a prefill), and Draft then resets the drafter's state to a fresh Start() and commits the priming token; ConstrainedDecoder::UpdateState is not called during MTP rounds and advances only on plain decode steps. Within a decode task with MTP on those are the priming step and, since 3fa97211, the plain steps MtpRoundFitsCache forces at the cache's end, where ConstrainedDecoder's state has not followed the rounds; what those steps mask was not traced.
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: DecodeLogitsImpl (executor 1670-1700): UpdateState only when last_run_is_decode, then ProcessLogits; Decode (1415-1480) passes the constraint to Draft and never calls UpdateState in a round; Draft (drafter 1303-1340) Start() + ComputeMask + ComputeNext(priming token). constrained_decoder.cc unchanged from Google's base. New since the old pin: 3fa97211 (2026-10-24, in the release) makes plain steps at the cache end with MTP on, which call UpdateState on a state that missed the rounds' tokens; not traced further. Corrected to say so.

text: Consequence: in the release Agello ships (agello-one-20261115), with speculative decoding on and an llguidance constraint (a JSON schema or a regex response format), a reply can leave the grammar: the drafts are masked from the right states, but a rejection's bonus token is picked under the mask of the position after d3, and a rejected draft stays committed in the matcher, so later masks come from a wrong state; this is consistent with the symptoms Agello recorded on device (garbled output or 'compute_mask() called after stop', LM-SWIFT-059), so MTP must stay off for constrained conversations with the release. Our build fixes both faults (ours: 1382157b, 2026-11-17): each state has its own matcher, and each state's mask is computed once and kept, which also removes the 'compute_mask() called after stop' error of a mask asked for twice.
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17: release (6da75396): drafter 540-610 and 808-826 with Google's llg_constraint.cc (66-91), the mechanism of X-GAP-019 to 021. Our build: llg_constraint.cc:80-128 at b7b856a0, B4 (1382157b) clones per state and keeps each owner's mask (its message: llguidance computes a position's mask once and errors 'compute_mask() called after stop' when asked again); llg_constraint_test StatesStayIndependentAcrossARound covers it. Old text said 'documented build and v0.18.0' and 'report upstream'; rewritten per build, no upstream step.
original_text: Consequence: with speculative decoding on and an llguidance constraint (a JSON schema or a regex response format), the documented build and the v0.18.0 source can emit tokens the grammar doesn't allow: a rejection's bonus token is picked under the mask of the position after d3, and a rejected draft stays committed in the matcher; this matches Agello's on-device observation (LM-SWIFT-059), so MTP must stay off for constrained conversations at the pin too, and it is a correctness bug to report upstream.

text: Agello (a69121286e) starts a chat reply only when maxNumTokens minus the tokens the cache will hold after the message's prefill (counted exactly for text) and a 64-token margin leaves at least 96 tokens, and caps the reply at that room (ToolBudget.plan's share of it when tools are offered). Its maxNumTokens is always the positions LiteRT-LM allocates (ContextBudget.allocatedPositions: 32,000 for a request of 32,003 or more with the published file, the 64K window of 12 GB devices included), and the window is no longer a setting, so with exact counts a send's prefill has at least its input plus 160 positions free, more than the at most input + 127 that E4B's prefill_128 runs need, and a reply without tool calls stops decoding 64 positions before the end of the window plus at most one MTP round's tokens. At Agello 93122b6 (2026-10-15) a manual KV-cache size of 32,768 (the Stepper's top) allocated only 32,000 positions while the budget counted 32,768, so the margin didn't hold.
formula: room = maxNumTokens - used - input - 64 >= 96 -> free positions before the prefill = maxNumTokens - used >= input + 160; a 128-run plan needs ceil(L / 128) x 128 <= L + 127; decode stops at used + input + room = maxNumTokens - 64, overshot by at most 4 tokens of one round
verifier_note: Re-pin 2026-11-17, reconciliation r3, at Agello HEAD a69121286e. Margin arithmetic unchanged: room = w - used - 64 >= 96 with used = cached + message tokens (tokensAfterPrefill, exact for text), so free positions >= input + 160 > input + 127. New: resolve() passes every request, override included, through allocatedPositions (exportWindow 32,003 -> (32003-1)/256*256 = 32,000; 65,536 -> 32,000), and DeviceProfile (71-89) makes the window a fixed 16K or 64K, no longer a setting (2026-11-02), so the 32,768 caveat is history (AdvancedSettingsView and InferencePlanner at 93122b6 kept as its sources); the Advanced screen was removed on 2026-11-11. Dropped 'so it stays clear of the positions an MTP round can reach past the end': since 3fa97211 no round runs past the end (X-GAP-010). The magic-number source is the ledger's, unchanged.
original_text: Agello (93122b6) starts a chat reply only when the window minus the tokens in use, the input estimate and a 64-token margin leaves at least 96 tokens, and caps the reply at that room; with exact counts, a send's prefill then has at least its input plus 160 positions free, more than the at most input + 127 that E4B's prefill_128 runs need, and its decode stops 64 positions before the end of the window plus at most one MTP round's tokens, so it stays clear of the positions an MTP round can reach past the end.
